title: Proposal to Ban Display, Slaughter and Sale of Wild-caught Soft-shelled Turtles at Wet Markets
what_it_is: Proposal to Ban Display, Slaughter and Sale of Wild-caught Soft-shelled Turtles at Wet Markets

sections.label: Wet market live turtle stalls
sections.summary: NEA stopped tendering wet market stalls for live turtle sales in 2012, but existing stalls may continue if they meet food safety and hygiene requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: NEA has stopped tendering out wet market stalls for the sale of live turtles since 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Existing wet market stalls that are currently allowed to slaughter and sell live turtles can, however, carry on with their trade if they comply with food safety and hygiene requirements under the Environmental Public Health Act.

sections.label: Low transmission risk assessment
sections.summary: Transmission risks are found to be low as long as food safety and hygiene standards are maintained.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Transmission risks are found to be low, as long as food safety and hygiene standards are maintained.

sections.label: Review of live animal sales
sections.summary: Agencies are reviewing the sale and slaughter of live animals in wet markets, considering international benchmarking and scientific evidence, and will continue improving public health and environmental hygiene standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, agencies are reviewing the sale and slaughter of live animals in wet markets taking into consideration international benchmarking and scientific evidence, and will continue with efforts to improve public health and environmental hygiene standards in Singapore, including our wet markets.

sections.label: Low risk, hygiene, agency roles
sections.summary: Risk is assessed as low but not zero; Salmonella can spread through touching and ingestion, so vendors and patrons must maintain hygiene, and NParks and SFA ensure CITES compliance and food safety standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Yes, so as I had said, risk is assessed to be low but just like in crime, low risk does not mean no risk.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And indeed, Salmonella is common in live animals and raw meat and can be transmitted through, like the Member has said, touching and through ingestion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, both the vendor as well as the patrons will have to ensure that they maintain good food safety and hygiene practices, which will include washing your hands with soap after touching the raw meat, as well as cooking it well to kill the harmful bacteria.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have noted, so far, we have not detected any cases of zoonotic disease transmission from the sale of this; but as I have said again, we are reviewing this currently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NParks would be involved in making sure that there is no CITES violation, for instance, for the import of such turtles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And SFA is involved in ensuring that the stalls in the wet markets comply with food safety and hygiene standards.
